title: TaskCompletionService
responsibility: Audits committed coding or planning evidence and refuses completion when verification, profiling or proposal checks are missing or stale.

inputs.name: TaskCompletionService.constructor.root
inputs.description: Project root directory that check() and require() use for Git reads, loop metadata, verification records and the audit record location. The constructor only stores it and does not check that it is a Git repository.

inputs.name: TaskCompletionService.check.input
inputs.description: Task metadata to audit: kind must be coding or planning, goal must be non-blank, and plan names a committed project-relative proposal that is audited for planning tasks or whenever plan is set; units are checked only for coding tasks and must exist at the audited commit. Uncommitted or untracked changes fail the source check, except the loop.json and trace.ndjson of the named loop when loop is set; with loop set, goal must equal the committed and current loop goal and the kind and plan must match any completion committed in loop.json.

examples.goal: Add a latency and memory profile to the evidence grid
Plan latency and memory evidence for the evidence grid

inputs.name: TaskCompletionService.requirePlan.proposal
inputs.description: Markdown proposal that planAudit parses but never executes: its sections must have titles matching overview, objective, scope or goal; acceptance or success criteria; dependencies; verification, testing or validation; and performance, each with at least 12 characters of body. The acceptance section needs a bullet item, the performance section must mention a workload (or representative or scenario), latency (or timing or response time) and memory (or RSS), and no line may start with TODO, TBD, FIXME or 'Describe the user-facing outcome' in any letter case, optionally after a list marker.
examples:
# Evidence grid latency and memory plan

## Overview
Add a latency and memory evidence grid that shows each representative workload for the evidence grid view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The grid lists every representative workload with its measured latency.
- The grid reports resident memory (RSS) beside each latency value.

## Dependencies
The grid reads the committed verification record through the existing evidence repository.

## Verification
Run the automated tests for the grid, then run harness task check against the committed source.

## Performance
Measure a representative workload with a declared scenario, recording latency and memory (RSS) for each grid cell. No runtime results are recorded until the code runs.

inputs.name: TaskCompletionService.requirePlan.goal
inputs.description: Task goal used by the plan.request check: it must be non-blank, and if it has words of four or more characters other than please, should, could, would, with, that, this, task and plan, at least one of them must appear in the proposal. The match is a case-insensitive substring test.
examples: Plan latency and memory evidence for the evidence grid
Add a latency and memory profile to the evidence grid

outputs.name: TaskCompletionService.check
outputs.description: The audit record, also written as <id>.json under the Git directory's harness/task-audits (or a temporary directory when Git cannot resolve that path), with passed true only when every check passed. Source, plan, code and verification problems become failed checks instead of being thrown, and commit is null when the first source audit throws.

outputs.name: taskCompletionInstructions
outputs.description: The four fixed guidance strings, returned in the same order on every call: coding profiling, committing with harness verify and harness task check, planning-only sections, and the limits of the heuristic audit.
examples: Coding tasks require actual representative latency and memory profiling through Harness, independently of budget declarations. Use PerformanceProfileService in standardized tests or harness budget bench with a declared workload; label whole-process memory honestly.

Commit the task source, run harness verify run --require-performance, then harness task check --loop <loop>. Missing, failed or stale evidence blocks completion; an agent reply or a free-text step claim is not verification.

Planning tasks remain planning-only: include substantive Overview, Acceptance Criteria, Dependencies, Verification and Performance sections, with representative workloads, latency and memory measurement plans. Run the Harness task audit; do not fabricate runtime results or implement the plan.

The final audit checks structural and evidence heuristics, not arbitrary semantic correctness. Expose remaining uncertainty and obtain required acceptance review. Do not change source after auditing it or claim completion while the audit fails.

errors.name: Task completion audit failed
errors.description: Thrown by requirePlan() and require() as 'Task completion audit failed: ' followed by the failed check details (space-separated for requirePlan(), one per line for require()); check() and require() also reject when the audit record cannot be written.
